title: Third moves other than 3.Nc3
intro:
After 2...Qxd5 almost everyone plays 3.Nc3, because it develops with a hit on the queen and there is no reason not to. This chapter is the rest: White develops something else first, or takes the centre first, or offers a queen trade. In every case Black plays the same setup, and in most cases the game becomes chapter 1 by move six.

## The one choice

Against 3.Nf3 the knight comes to f6, and the pin on g4 is refused in a sentence: it is a good move and it commits the bishop before White has shown where the knight on b1 is going, and if that knight goes to c3 with a hit on the queen the bishop on g4 is a move Black may wish it had back. The knight to f6 keeps every option, and the pin comes a move later.

## What the others give up

3.d4 takes the centre first and usually transposes. 3.Be2 is quiet and blocks nothing, and it leaves the pawn on g2 to the queen: this is the one line in the course where the queen goes and takes something, because it can come back to g6 a pawn up with nothing to answer for. 3.Qf3 offers a queen trade, and Black takes it: with the queens off there is no tempo to lose and the structure with the pawn on c6 plays itself. 3.d3 is the small centre, and the pawn to c6 and the bishop to f5 are the answer, as against every quiet move in this course.

## Typical mistakes at this level

Declining the queen trade after 3.Qf3, which keeps the queen on d5 as a target for a knight that has not yet moved. Pinning on g4 before the knight on g8 has moved. Playing ...e6 before the bishop is out. Declining a free pawn on g2 after 3.Be2 in order to develop, when the queen can take it and come home. And chasing the main line when a quiet move has been played: against 3.d3 there is nothing to punish, and the right answer is to develop and be comfortable.

children.plan: Meet Nc3 with the pawn to c6 so the knight has no b5, then the bishop to f5, the knight to d7 and the pawn to e6, and the king castles when the queenside is quiet. The pawn is kept and the position is the usual one with an extra pawn.
